decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state file exists for this work. In Section 4.2 (Results), Polman (2025) empirically tests whether the happiness-spending association in the new field sample (N = 307 undergraduates given $10 to spend) is moderated by utilitarian vs. indulgent product ratings, directly testing the negative association (sadder/less happy individuals spending more on utilitarian products such as a water bottle) reported by Cryder et al. (2008). Using floodlight analysis, the study finds a significant negative association between happiness and spending for utilitarian products (rating <= 2.34) and explicitly concludes in Results that 'our study replicates both Babin and Darden’s findings and Lerner et al.’s and Cryder et al.’s findings.' The reference list (lines 388-391) identifies Cryder, C. E., Lerner, J. S., Gross, J. J., & Dahl, R. E. (2008), 'Misery is not miserly: Sad and self-focused individuals spend more,' Psychological Science, 19, 525-530 (no DOI printed in source). The only shipped row (input_row_index 388) is Babin & Darden (1996, Journal of Business Research, 35, 201-206, DOI 10.1016/0148-2963(95)00125-5), and sibling target_index 2 is Lerner, Small, & Loewenstein (2004, Psychological Science, 15, 337-341); both are distinct independent studies rather than alternate reports of Cryder et al. (2008).

In Section 4.2 (Results), Polman (2025) empirically retests the finding of Lerner, Small, & Loewenstein (2004) that sadness increases spending on utilitarian goods (such as a highlighter) by regressing real-life spending on dispositional happiness, product utilitarian/indulgent ratings, and their interaction (N = 307), followed by a floodlight decomposition showing a significant negative happiness-spending slope for utilitarian items (rating <= 2.34). The Results section explicitly concludes that 'our study replicates both Babin and Darden’s findings and Lerner et al.’s and Cryder et al.’s findings.' The reference list (lines 469-472) identifies Lerner, J. S., Small, D. A., & Loewenstein, G. (2004), 'Heart strings and purse strings: Carryover effects of emotions on economic decisions,' Psychological Science, 15, 337-341 (no DOI printed in source). This work is absent from the shipped dataset, whose only row (input_row_index 388) is Babin & Darden (1996, DOI 10.1016/0148-2963(95)00125-5), and it is an independent study distinct from sibling target_index 1 (Cryder et al., 2008).
